title: Unified SDK error adapter and hinting layer for retries & streaming ergonomics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Current SDKs (Python/TS/Go) expose inconsistent exception types and error payloads. Product and infra teams keep adding ad hoc retry logic in callers because SDK errors do not carry unified retry/backoff hints or streaming backpressure signals. This ticket proposes an SDK-level 'error adapter' layer that normalizes server error codes into language-idiomatic exceptions with structured, human-friendly messages and machine-friendly hint fields (retriable, retry_after, backoff_hint_ms, streaming_close_reason).
proposal: Introduce an SDK-level adapter that maps raw HTTP/gRPC error payloads into a small, stable set of exception classes per language: TransientError, PermanentError, RateLimitError, StreamClosedError, PayloadValidationError.

Attach non-nested metadata fields to exceptions: 'code' (string), 'retriable' (boolean), 'retry_after' (RFC3339 or seconds), 'backoff_hint_ms' (integer), 'hint' (short message). These should be accessible as attributes (py: e.code, ts: e.code, go: e.Code()).

Define 'streaming ergonomics' for partial results: on StreamClosedError include 'final_offset' (if applicable) and 'resume_token' when available. SDK should expose a helper that wraps stream iterators and translates server close signals to RetryableResumeHint where appropriate.

Ensure default SDK retry behavior uses the adapter hints: By default SDKs will perform at most 3 automatic retries for errors where retriable=true, obeying retry_after and exponential backoff guided by backoff_hint_ms. Callers can opt out and implement custom policies.

Provide migration guides and lint rules: developers get warnings when they inspect raw HTTP payloads instead of using adapter exceptions. Document mapping table from server codes to SDK exception classes.
Emit structured telemetry: each exception thrown should include a stable telemetry tag derived from 'code' and 'retriable' to simplify SLO dashboards and alerting.
milestones: Language-specific adapter impls (week 2-3): python, typescript, go
Docs, migration guide, and feature flag rollout (week 5)
acceptance_criteria: All three SDKs throw language-idiomatic exceptions for the same server error codes according to the mapping table.
Exceptions expose attributes: code, retriable, retry_after (when supplied), backoff_hint_ms, hint. No nested JSON fields in exception attributes.
Default automatic retry honors retriable flag and respects retry_after/backoff_hint_ms. Tests simulate server-side Retry-After headers and custom error payloads.
Streaming wrapper converts abrupt server stream closures into StreamClosedError with resume_token when available and provides a helper to transparently resume for idempotent workloads.
End-to-end integration tests and unit tests covering 10 representative server error payloads.
Documentation: README, per-language migration snippet, changelog entry, and a short blog-style note describing developer ergonomics improvements.
Telemetry: new metric 'sdk.error_adapter.mapped' emitted with tags code=<code> and retriable=<true|false>, visible in console-qa dashboard.
implementation_tasks: Create canonical mapping table document (contrib: runtime/errors.md)
Python: implement ErrorAdapter class, new exceptions module, integrate with existing http client retry middleware, update SDK config to enable/disable auto-retry
TypeScript: implement ErrorAdapter, export typed Error interfaces with code & retriable fields, update fetch/got wrapper used by SDK, provide helper to compose retry policies
Go: add errors package with mapped types and accessor methods, ensure compatibility with existing error wrapping in go-sdk
Streaming: implement StreamWrapper abstraction in each SDK that yields items and raises StreamClosedError with resume_token; include examples for 'resume on idempotent' and 'fail-fast' modes
Backwards compatibility: add feature flag 'use_error_adapter' default true; provide fallbacks to legacy behavior if false
Add unit tests for mapping, attribute exposure, retry scheduling, and streaming resume scenarios
Add e2e tests using the test server that emits synthetic errors including rate-limit with Retry-After and invalid payload responses
Docs: write migration guide, add examples, update CHANGELOG & SDK release notes
examples:
Python example: 
from redwood import Client, errors
try:
    client.generate('hello')
except errors.RateLimitError as e:
    print(e.code, e.retriable, e.retry_after)
    # fallback to cached answer or queue request

Streaming resume snippet (python): 
for chunk in client.stream_generate(prompt, resume_on_retry=True):
  process(chunk)
# if StreamClosedError is raised, helper will attempt resume when safe
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit counter sdk.error_adapter.mapped with tag 'code' and 'retriable'
Emit histogram sdk.error_adapter.retry_delay_ms for actual backoff delays used by SDK auto-retry
Log structured event when StreamClosedError includes resume_token (field: resume_token_present=true)
Add dashboard in console: 'SDK Error Adapter — mapping & retries' showing top codes, retry rates, and success after retry
dependencies: runtime:server-error-schema (will publish canonical error payloads and codes)
qa:test-server - updated to emit synthetic error payloads
risks: Breaking change risk if callers relied on raw HTTP error shapes; mitigated via feature flag and migration guide
Mismatch between server error vocabulary and adapter mapping could lead to incorrect retry behavior; mitigated by canonical mapping doc and integration tests
Potential for silent repeated retries if retriable flag is mis-set; mitigate by conservative default retry limits and telemetry alerts
testing_plan: Unit tests for mapping table coverage (>=10 server codes)
Property tests for retry timing and jitter heuristics
Integration tests: run client against test server scenarios: 429 with Retry-After, 503 transient, 400 invalid payload
Streaming tests: simulated connection resets with resume_token and without, verify resume helper behavior
Canary release: roll out Python SDK to 5% of traffic behind feature flag, monitor sdk.error_adapter.mapped and retry_success_ratio
notes: Reviewed initial design with runtime and product on 2026-02-28; runtime asked for a stable 'code' string field in server payloads
PM feedback: prefer short human hint strings for logs and long-form doc for engineers
Design decision: do not attempt to carry nested 'causes' field in exception to keep exception attributes language-friendly
Follow-up: add lint rule in SDK repo to detect direct parsing of raw server error responses in user-land code
